He played [[college basketball]] for [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]]. ==Early life== Woodard grew up playing [[basketball]] and [[baseball]] but narrowed his focus to basketball by the time he started high school, in part due to his exceptional height.{{cite web |last1=Lowery |first1=Logan |title=Woodard's basketball focus paying off |url=https://www.djournal.com/sports/woodard-s-basketball-focus-paying-off/article_f4f33ddd-5511-58d8-8f08-23868876d8d5.html |website=[[Northeast Mississippi Daily Journal]] |access-date=December 19, 2019 |date=February 8, 2019}} He was already receiving Division I college attention in eighth grade. He played basketball for [[Columbus High School (Mississippi)|Columbus High School]] in [[Columbus, Mississippi]].{{cite web |last1=Faulk |first1=Robbie |title=Robert Woodard Sr. "Elated" in Son's Decision |url=https://247sports.com/college/mississippi-state/Article/Robert-Woodard-Sr-Elated-in-Sons-Decision-110634869/ |website=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=December 19, 2019 |date=November 24, 2017}} As a sophomore, Woodard led Columbus to its first Mississippi Class 6A state title after averaging 20.2 points, 7.1 rebounds and four assists per game.{{cite web |last1=Sammon |first1=Will |title=Luther Riley out as Columbus basketball coach |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/high-school/2016/06/10/luther-riley-out-columbus-basketball-coach/85641382/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |access-date=December 19, 2019 |date=June 10, 2016}} In his junior season, he averaged 25.2 points, 13.1 rebounds, 3.2 assists and three blocks per game and was named Mississippi [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]].{{cite web |last1=Costabile |first1=Annie |title=Robert Woodard named Gatorade POY |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/sports/high-school/2017/03/20/columbus-robert-woodard-named-gatorade-player-year/99422174/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |access-date=December 19, 2019 |date=March 20, 2017}} As a senior, Woodard won his second Class 6A state championship and repeated as Mississippi Gatorade Player of the Year. A four-star [[college recruiting|recruit]] and the highest-rated prospect in his state, he committed to play [[college basketball]] for [[Mississippi State Bulldogs men's basketball|Mississippi State]] over offers from [[Alabama Crimson Tide men's basketball|Alabama]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]] and [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]], among others.{{cite web |title=Four-star forward Robert Woodard commits to Mississippi State |url=https://www.wjtv.com/sports/four-star-forward-robert-woodard-commits-to-mississippi-state/ |website=[[WJTV]] |access-date=December 19, 2019 |date=November 15, 2017}} ==College career== As a freshman, Woodard averaged 5.5 points and 4.1 rebounds per game in 17.4 minutes per game. He started one contest and shot 46 percent on field goals. He spent the following summer working on his shooting and lifting weights. On November 17, 2019, Woodard set career highs with 21 points and 16 rebounds in an 82–59 win over [[New Orleans Privateers men's basketball|New Orleans]].{{cite news |title=Woodard sends Mississippi State past New Orleans 82-59 |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401169835 |access-date=December 25, 2019 |work=[[ESPN]] |agency=[[Associated Press]] |date=November 17, 2019}} As a sophomore, Woodard averaged 11.4 points and 6.5 rebounds per game.{{cite news |title=S. Carolina, Miss. St. meet in conference play |url=https://apnews.com/bcbee7cc70104514b9036046d7617687 |access-date=March 19, 2020 |work=[[Associated Press]] |date=February 18, 2020}} Following the season, Woodard declared for the [[2020 NBA draft]], with the intention of remaining in the draft.{{cite news |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=Mississippi State's Robert Woodard II entering NBA draft |url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/29016177/mississippi-state-robert-woodard-ii-entering-nba-draft |access-date=April 9, 2020 |work=[[ESPN]] |date=April 9, 2020}} He had career totals of 539 points, 53 steals, 49 blocks, 65 assists and 342 rebounds.{{cite news |last1=Palmer |first1=Lydia |title=From MSU to the NBA: Robert Woodard II |url=http://www.reflector-online.com/sports/article_7ec32e4a-f51d-11ea-b04d-3b88334598bf.html |access-date=October 5, 2020 |work=The Reflector |date=September 13, 2020}} ==Professional career== ===Sacramento / Stockton Kings / Austin Spurs (2020–2022)=== Woodard was selected by the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] with the 40th pick in the [[2020 NBA draft]]. He was subsequently traded alongside a 2022 second-round draft selection to the [[Sacramento Kings]] in exchange for [[Xavier Tillman]].{{cite web |title=Kings Acquire Draft Rights To Robert Woodard II and 2022 Second-Round Draft Selection |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-draft-rights-robert-woodard-ii-and-2022-second-round-draft-selection |website=NBA.com |access-date=November 21, 2020 |date=November 19, 2020}} On December 1, 2020, Woodard was signed by the Kings.{{cite web |title=Kings Sign Robert Woodard II |url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-sign-robert-woodard-ii |website=NBA.com |access-date=December 1, 2020 |date=December 1, 2020}} On February 1, 2021, it was announced Woodard would have his first assignment at the [[NBA G League]] for the [[Austin Spurs]].{{cite web|title=Austin Spurs receive flex-assignment Robert Woodard II from Sacramento Kings|url=https://austin.gleague.nba.com/news/austin-spurs-receive-flex-assignment-robert-woodard-ii-from-sacramento-kings|date=February 1, 2021|website=NBA.com|access-date=February 1, 2021}} On January 5, 2022, Woodard was assigned to the [[Stockton Kings]] after suffering an undisclosed illness.{{cite news |title=Kings' Robert Woodard: Returns to action in G League |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/kings-robert-woodard-returns-to-action-in-g-league/ |access-date=January 6, 2022 |work=[[CBS Sports]] |date=January 6, 2022}} On February 10, he was waived by the Kings.{{Cite web|title=Kings Acquire Donte DiVincenzo, Josh Jackson and Trey Lyles in Four-Team Deal|url=https://www.nba.com/kings/news/kings-acquire-donte-divincenzo-josh-jackson-and-trey-lyles-four-team-deal|access-date=February 10, 2022|website=NBA}} ===Oklahoma City Blue (2022–2023)=== On February 19, 2022, Woodard was acquired via waivers by the [[Iowa Wolves]].{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|date=February 19, 2022|access-date=February 19, 2022}} Two days later, Woodard was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Blue]] in exchange for [[Melvin Frazier]].{{cite web|title=2021-22 NBA G League Transactions|url=https://gleague.nba.com/transactions/|website=NBA.com|date=February 21, 2022|access-date=February 21, 2022}} On March 4, 2022, Woodard signed a [[two-way contract]] with the [[San Antonio Spurs]].{{cite web|title=The Spurs have signed Robert Woodard II and D.J. Stewart Jr. to two-way contracts|url=https://www.poundingtherock.com/2022/3/4/22962268/the-spurs-have-signed-robert-woodard-ii-and-d-j-stewart-jr-to-two-way-contracts|website=PoundingTheRock.com|date=March 4, 2022|access-date=March 4, 2022}} On October 4, 2022, Woodard signed with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]]. On October 7, Woodard was waived after appearing in one pre season game. On November 3, 2022, Woodard was named to the opening night roster for the [[Oklahoma City Blue]].{{cite web|title=Oklahoma City Blue Roster 2022-23|url=https://oklahomacity.gleague.nba.com/roster|website=NBA.com|date=November 3, 2022|access-date=November 3, 2022}} ===ADA Blois (2023)=== On August 2, 2023, Woodard signed with [[ADA Blois Basket 41|ADA Blois]] of the French [[LNB Pro A|Betclic Élite]].{{cite web|title=ROBERT WOODARD II DERNIÈRE PIÈCE DU PUZZLE!|url=http://ada-basket.com/2023/08/02/robert-woodard-ii-derniere-piece-puzzle/|website=ADA-Basket.com|date=August 2, 2023|access-date=August 2, 2023|language=French}} ===Maroussi (2023–2024)=== On December 17, 2023, Woodard signed with Greek club [[Maroussi B.C.|Maroussi]] for the rest of the season.{{Cite news |last=Maggi |first=Alessandro |date=2023-12-17 |title=Maroussi signs Robert Woodard - Sportando |url=https://sportando.basketball/en/maroussi-signs-robert-woodard/ |access-date=2024-03-21 |work=Sportando |language=en-US}} ===Memphis Hustle (2024–2025)=== On October 28, 2024, Woodard joined the [[Memphis Hustle]].{{cite web|title=Memphis Hustle announce 2024–25 Training Camp Roster|url=https://memphis.gleague.nba.com/news/memphis-hustle-announce-2024-25-training-camp-roster|website=NBA.com|date=October 28, 2024|access-date=October 28, 2024}} ===Delaware Blue Coats (2025)=== On January 6, 2025, Woodard was traded to the [[Delaware Blue Coats]].{{cite tweet|author=Delaware Blue Coats|title=OFFICIAL: the Delaware Blue Coats acquire Robert Woodard II from the Memphis Hustle. To complete the trade, Delaware sends Max Fiedler to the Texas Legends, and Memphis receives a 2025 2nd round pick from the College Park Skyhawks. welcome to DE, Robert!👋|number=1876426542034612312|user=blue_coats|date=January 6, 2025|access-date=January 7, 2025}} ===Maine Celtics (2025–present)=== On December 19, 2025, the [[Maine Celtics]] announced that they had signed Woodard.{{cite web|title=Maine Celtics sign Robert Woodard II|url=https://maine.gleague.nba.com/news/maine-celtics-sign-robert-woodard-ii-12182025|date=December 19, 2025|website=NBA.com|access-date=December 19, 2025}} ==National team career== Woodard won a gold medal with the [[United States men's national under-16 basketball team|United States]] at the [[2015 FIBA Americas Under-16 Championship]] in [[Bahía Blanca]], Argentina. He played in all five games and averaged 5.6 points and 3.8 rebounds per game.{{cite web |last1=Cronin |first1=Courtney |title=Woodard, USA Basketball win gold at FIBA Americas |url=https://www.clarionledger.com/story/prepsreport/2015/06/15/robert-woodard-fiba-americas/71253188/ |website=[[The Clarion-Ledger]] |access-date=December 19, 2019 |date=June 15, 2015}} ==Career
